parts:
Hi, 
I am running my stan code in R. and here comes the memory size issue. 
Sorry, I only keep a photo of the error message. It is in attachment.
Below is my code:


M1_code<-"
data{   #get the data we have
int <lower=0> N; #number of obs
int <lower=0> J; #number of gene level 
vector[N] y ; #y
vector[N] x; #x
int <lower=1,upper=J> gene[N];
}
parameters{ #specify the parameter we want to know 
vector[J] a;  #random intercept when gene is the level 
real mu_a;  #mean for intercept
real <lower=0> sigma_a;  #variance of intercept
real <lower=0> sigma_y; #population variance
real beta;    #common slope;

}
transformed parameters{ #specify the model we will use 
vector[N] y_hat;
for (i in 1:N) 
     y_hat[i] <- a[gene[i]]+beta*x[i];#specify the group
}
model { #give the prior distribution 
  beta ~ normal(0,10);
  mu_a ~ normal(0,100);
  a ~ normal(mu_a, sigma_a);
  y ~ normal(y_hat, sigma_y); #y and y_hat should have same type 
}
"

N<-dim(table)[1]

x=table$envarp,gene=index)

Is it a R memory issue or Stan memory issue?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: memory size issue
parts:
On Friday, August 7, 2015 at 11:18:23 AM UTC-4, shuaiqi zhang wrote:
I am running my stan code in R. and here comes the memory size issue.
RStan is not really optimized for memory, but ...

transformed parameters{ #specify the model we will use 
vector[N] y_hat;
for (i in 1:N) 
     y_hat[i] <- a[gene[i]]+beta*x[i];#specify the group
}

Do you really need the posterior distribution of y_hat for all N observations? If not, put all that inside the model block so that it is not stored. If necessary, you could recreate it inside R fairly easily from the posterior distribution of a and beta.

Ben
